_comment: Registration for scripts/check-cpp-host-writes.py (issue #1132).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it lets work THROUGH.
`make verify` and the CI step read its green as 'every host write in the two
cpp command documents goes through the seam', and nothing downstream
re-derives it. A blind version reports the same clean line over the
half-seamed state #1139 shipped, where a defer-set naming ~/.bashrc refused
two writes, printed a stated refusal, and wrote the file anyway.
FOUR WRITE FORMS, ONE CASE EACH, because every enumeration BY SURFACE in
this issue missed something and the forms are what the gate actually reads.
THE FIFTH AND SIXTH CASES TEST THE FILTER ITSELF. A comment filter is not a
neutral refinement - it is a new way to be blind, so it needs both
directions: a comment must not red, and a write that merely LOOKS like one
must. Without the sixth, the obvious `"#" in line` implementation passes
every other case in this register.
POPULATION: the gate scans two documents and says so in its verdict. It
claims nothing about the other command families, which are not in its input.
Stdlib-only and git-free, like the gate: nothing here is absent from the
slim CI image, so the control gives the same verdict there as here.
A CASE THAT WAS WRITTEN AND THEN REMOVED: `bad-same-line-redirect`. The
anchor CATCHES it, because a same-line redirect is the one form the first
framing did implement, so the case cannot distinguish the gate from the
blind version. A case whose expected answer BOTH sides produce demonstrates
nothing about the difference between them - the same trap that nearly
shipped in #1139's control. The form is still exercised on every run, by the
real documents.

cases.name: bad-indirect-shell
cases.why: The target is assigned $HOME on one line and written eight lines later. This is the shape that hid two ~/.bashrc writes through #1139 and a review: the verb and the path never share a line, so every same-line survey reported the file clean.

cases.name: bad-embedded-python
cases.why: A write_text() inside a python heredoc. Satisfies no grep for a redirect, cp, tee, mv or ln, which is why ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json was absent from three successive enumerations.

cases.name: bad-mkdir
cases.why: mkdir -p of a host directory. A directory is a surface: a defer-set naming ~/.claude must refuse its creation, not fall through to a permission error.

cases.name: bad-hash-inside-a-string
cases.why: THE FILTER'S OWN BAD CASE. printf '# managed by cpp' >> "$RC" is a real write whose line contains a hash inside a string. A comment filter written as `"#" in line` - the obvious first version - excuses it, and a block appended to a shell rc almost always carries exactly such a banner. The filter added to remove false positives is a new way to be blind, and this is the direction nobody re-checks.

cases.name: good-writes-only-in-comments
cases.why: Every write FORM present, each inside a real comment, plus one harmless echo. Three false positives in this issue's own analysis came from quoting a write in prose, so the filter must exist; this case is what stops it being removed, and it is byte-adjacent to the bad case above so the pair isolates the filter's rule rather than its existence.

anchors.note: Constructed, so --verify-provenance reports unverified, which is correct and must never be read as ok.
anchors.why: The framing this issue actually started from: grep for a redirect to a $HOME path, and treat any line containing a hash as a comment. It misses all four bad cases and each was a real miss before it was a fixture - the indirect form hid two ~/.bashrc writes through #1139 and a review, embedded python hid opencode.json from three enumerations, mkdir was never counted as a surface, and the naive filter excuses a banner line. It agrees on the good case, which is what keeps the demonstration isolated.
